questions.q: What job does the amygdala perform in the brain, according to the summary?
a: It spots threats within milliseconds, though often inaccurately
It calms aggression and enables rational thought
It stores long-term memories and language
It coordinates movement and balance
questions.why: The summary pairs the fast, fearful amygdala with the slower, rational frontal cortex.

questions.q: What happened to Phineas Gage after an iron rod destroyed his frontal cortex?
a: His personality changed and he suffered violent mood swings
He lost the ability to speak or understand words
He forgot his family and his past entirely
He became unusually calm and agreeable
questions.why: Without his frontal cortex restraining the amygdala, Gage could not control his aggression.

questions.q: What does the summary say happens when white people briefly view faces of another race?
a: The amygdala fires first, then the frontal cortex calms it
The frontal cortex fires first, then the amygdala reacts
Both brain regions remain inactive during the viewing
The amygdala stays active for several minutes afterward
questions.why: The fear response lasts a split second before the frontal cortex quells it in non-racists.

questions.q: How does the presence of women change male behavior, according to the summary?
a: Men take more risks and buy more expensive things
Men speak more quietly and avoid eye contact
Men become more generous and share credit
Men focus more carefully on the task at hand
questions.why: The summary attributes this to mating signals in the male brain.

questions.q: How do individualists and collectivists differ when recalling a complex scene?
a: Individualists recall the person; collectivists recall the setting
Individualists recall the setting; collectivists recall the person
Both groups recall the same mix of person and setting
Both groups recall only the faces in the scene
questions.why: The summary says culture shapes which details of a scene people notice and remember.
